transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um... I guess I just need some help with... my thoughts. I drive a cab, and... well, even when I know I already did my safety check, this thought just keeps hitting me that I missed something on the car. Like... somebody could get hurt, or my boss is gonna say I lied about checking it. 

It's just... I can't make it shut up. It just keeps going while I'm driving, or... or when I'm trying to study. It just won't stop.
Do these thoughts about missing something on the car feel like they are coming into your mind against your will?

Yeah... um... like I said, I just can't make it shut up. I don't want to be thinking about the cab or... or people getting hurt. It just... it hits me anyway. I'm not trying to think about it. It just happens.
Do you find yourself doing anything over and over to try to make these thoughts about missing something on the car go away?

Um... yeah. I guess I do. Before I can take a ride, I... I end up walking around the car. A lot. Just... checking the tires, the lights, the doors. The meter, my paperwork. I just keep doing it. Over and over. 

Sometimes I... um... I take pictures of them on my phone. And if it doesn't feel right, I... I have to restart the whole check. It's... it's embarrassing, honestly. Because I'll do it even when passengers are standing right there waiting for me, and I'm already late. I just... I have to do it anyway.
Do you feel less anxious after you've finished walking around the car and checking everything?
Um... yeah. A little, I guess. But... it doesn't really last long.
Are you walking around the car and checking everything to try to prevent something bad from happening?

Yeah... I guess so. Like I was saying, that's why I keep doing all that... checking the tires and the lights and taking the pictures. Even with the passengers standing right there. I just... I don't want to miss something and cause a crash or... yeah. I just have to be sure.
Is checking the car and taking pictures mostly to make yourself feel less anxious or mostly to actually prevent an accident from happening?

Um... I don't really know. Maybe... both? 

Like I just said, before I take a ride, I just have to keep going around checking everything. The doors, the paperwork, taking those pictures... and if it feels wrong, I have to restart the whole thing. Even if I'm late and they're waiting. I do it to make sure nothing bad happens, but... yeah, doing it makes that bad feeling go away for a minute, too. I just... I have to do it.
Is the feeling that you need to keep checking the car mostly because you're afraid something bad will happen, or mostly because you feel anxious if you don't do it?

I mean... like I just said, I'm not really sure which one it is. 

I just know that before I can take a ride, I have to keep checking everything. The tires, the lights... the doors, the meter, the paperwork. Just over and over. Taking the pictures. If it doesn't feel right, I have to restart the whole thing. Even with the passengers waiting right there and I'm already late. I just... I have to do it. So maybe it's the anxious thing. I don't know.
Is the main reason you repeat the checks to stop the anxious feeling or to actually make sure nothing bad happens?

I don't know... I've told you this already. It's just... I have to do it. 

I just... I check the tires, the lights, the doors, the meter, the paperwork. Over and over. I take the pictures. If it doesn't feel right, I start over. Even if people are waiting. I just... I don't know why exactly. I just have to.
Is the feeling of relief you get from checking the car mostly because you feel like you've prevented something bad from happening?

Look, I... I really don't know. I'm not trying to be difficult, it's just... I don't think about it like that. 

I just do the checks, and then I can drive. That's... that's all I know. I just have to do it.
Is the relief you feel after checking the car more about feeling safe or more about feeling less anxious?

I... I really don't know how else to answer this. I don't sit there and analyze how I feel after. 

It just means I can finally put the car in gear. That's it.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check the car repeatedly if you didn't feel anxious about missing something?

I... I don't know. I've never really... not felt that way. So I couldn't tell you. 

I just know I have to check. That's all.
Would you say that you're checking the car to make sure everything is okay, or to make yourself feel better?

I... I don't really see the difference, honestly. 

I just check it so I can start my shift. I'm not really paying attention to whether it's for the car or... or for me. It's just what I have to do.
Do you think the bad things you're afraid might happen would still worry you if you didn't have these repeating thoughts about them?

I mean... I don't know. The thoughts are the problem. That's... that's why I'm here. 

Even when I know I did the safety check on the cab, the thought just keeps hitting me... over and over... that I missed something. That someone's gonna get hurt, or my boss is gonna think I lied about doing the check. 

I just... I can't make it shut up. Not when I'm driving, not when I'm trying to study. It just doesn't stop.
Do you think the thoughts about missing something on the car would bother you as much if there were no consequences for missing something?

I... I guess I've never really thought about it like that. 

There's always consequences, though. In a car, anyway. So... I don't really know how to answer that. I just know the thoughts are there.
If you were absolutely certain that nothing bad would happen, would the thoughts about missing something on the car still bother you?

I... I don't know. 

I mean... if I knew for sure nothing bad would happen? I guess... maybe not? But I can't know that. So... I don't really know.
Do you think you would still check the car repeatedly if you didn't feel anxious about it, but still thought something bad might happen?

I... I don't know. Probably not. But I do feel anxious, so... I check. 

I just... before I can even take a ride, I have to go around the car. The tires, the lights, the doors... the meter, the paperwork. I just keep checking them. Over and over. Sometimes I take pictures on my phone just to... prove it to myself. If it doesn't feel right, I have to start the whole thing over. Even if... even if someone's waiting for me and I'm already running late. I just... I have to do it.
Is the main reason you check the car to prevent an accident or to stop feeling anxious?

I... I don't know. Both, maybe. 

I just... like I said, before I take a ride, I have to check everything. The tires, lights, the doors... the meter. I just go around the car, over and over. Sometimes I take pictures on my phone. And if... if it doesn't feel right, I have to start all over again. Even if people are waiting. I just have to.
Would you say that your main goal in checking the car is to make sure everything is safe?

I guess so. Yeah. Safety. 

But I mean... like I said, I just... I check it all. The tires, the meter, the doors. I take pictures of it. If it doesn't feel right, I just... I start over. Even if I'm late. I just do it.
Is the anxiety you feel when you haven't checked the car a result of thinking something bad might happen or is it more about feeling uneasy in general?

I... I'm not really sure. It's just... a bad feeling. Like something is wrong. 

I don't really know how to explain it. I just know I can't start driving until I... until I check everything again. It just feels wrong if I don't do it.
Is the reason you feel compelled to check the car mostly to reduce your own anxiety or mostly to prevent actual harm to others?
I don't know... I guess I just want the bad feeling to go away. I just... I don't want anything bad to happen, either. I don't really know which one it is. I just have to do it.
